author: macro-strategist-cyrus-daruwalla
description: Does the US real-rate (FRED DFII10) regime (rising vs falling, 3m change threshold +/-0.10pp) change whether VALUE (ff_beta_HML loading) or MOMENTUM (ff_beta_WML loading) earns a better cross-sectional IC on panel_long, 2005-2026, 21yr.
data: ALPHA_RANKER/rnd/panel/panel_long.parquet ff_beta_HML/ff_beta_WML loadings (proxy for style tilt -- no separate long-short factor-return series exists in this panel, disclosed as an [INFERENCE] proxy) + FRED DFII10 this session.
interpretation: Momentum (WML) loading has a robust, statistically significant positive IC in BOTH regimes (t=2.86 rising, t=2.37 falling) -- it works regardless of the real-rate direction. Value (HML) loading has NO reliable IC in either regime (neither t clears 1.96). The value-minus-momentum IC gap is -0.021 in rising-rate months vs -0.039 in falling-rate months -- momentum's edge narrows somewhat (not disappears, let alone flips) when real rates rise. [OPINION, directional only, not actionable at this magnitude].
overall_verdict: KILL for 'switch to value when real rates rise' as an actionable rule -- momentum dominates value in BOTH regimes at this cut; the classic value-outperforms-when-rates-rise rotation thesis is NOT confirmed on this panel and this proxy.
confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on the KILL (large sample, 89-99 independent months per regime, momentum's own robustness across regimes is itself a clean, well-powered result)
